title_en: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Proves Fans Still Love Panem After Gobbling Up $225 Million at the Box Office in Its Opening Weekend
summary_en: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took GTA 6 players off of their couches and into movie theaters with a staggering estimated box office total of $225 million in its opening weekend.
body_en:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took GTA 6 players off of their couches and into movie theaters with a staggering estimated box office total of $225 million in its opening weekend.
The latest prequel in Suzanne Collins' run of Hunger Games adaptations attracted more than just fans, pulling in a whopping $125 million domestically and $105 million internationally following its November 20 release date. It's an impressive debut that proved the dystopia franchise has more than enough staying power, even in the face of the biggest entertainment launch of all time .
Attracting moviegoers to take a break from Vice City this weekend was star Joseph Zada (We Were Liars), who stars as a young Haymitch Abernathy to tell the story of the Second Quarter Quell and the impact it had on the Hunger Games for all time. A brutal flick that IGN gave an 8/10 review , Sunrise on the Reaping is an adaptation of Collins' book of the same name, which originally released in March 2025. Its star-studded cast also includes Jesse Plemons (Game Night) as Plutarch Heavensbee, Ralph Fiennes (28 Years Later) as President Snow, Glenn Close (Fatal Attraction) as Drusilla Sickle, Mckenna Grace (Five Nights at Freddy's 2) as Maysilee Donner, and more.
"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is one of the strongest entries of the franchise because of its excellent performances," we said in our review, "especially Joseph Zada’s compassionate turn as young Haymitch. It also closes the story of Panem on a high note."
The mainline Hunger Games movies took a break after catching up with the Katniss Everdeen saga that began with Collins' books. The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, a novel focused on a teenage Coriolanus Snow, launched in 2020 and was adapted into a film of the same name in 2023. That project, which starred Billy the Kid's Tom Blyth, landed atop the box office upon its debut, though with decidedly softer results that saw its global opening weekend reach $98.5 million .
Sunrise on the Reaping has now brought the focus back to the good guys, and to much success. The new Hunger Games movie had a hefty production budget of $150 million, according to Variety . With plenty of time left in theaters before heavy hitters like Dune: Part 3 and Avengers: Doomsday sweep theaters mid-December, Lionsgate is almost certainly happy with its first few days.
Despite appealing enough to moviegoers to sneak in an explosive theatrical debut right under GTA's nose, there's actually no word on whether audiences will see a new story set in Panem anytime soon. Collins has not announced any additional books set in that universe as of right now, but with so many characters and stories ripe for exploration, it probably wouldn't be too much of a surprise to see The Hunger Games back in theaters at some point.
Elsewhere at the box office for the late November weekend was Johnny Depp's Ebenezer , which racked up another $22 million. The grim Christmas Carol reimagining earned $42 million worldwide when it premiered last weekend. IGN gave it a 6/10 review . The top five box office earners and their global totals for the weekend are as follows:
1. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ($225 million)
2. Ebenezer ($22 million)
3. Ramayana ($13.765 million)
4. I Play Rocky ($13.111 million)
5. The Cat in the Hat (10.55 million)
While we wait to see if Collins returns with another book, you can check out everything you need to know before seeing Sunrise on the Reaping . You can also read one IGN writer's explanation for why the movie commits the cardinal sin of prequels .
